title: spec: `collectFlowGraphs` hands out a `FlowGraph` whose `edges` can hold a non-record — the node side #16752 filtered, the edge side it did not
body:
Found while implementing #16910, which re-pointed the flow `edges` readers in `packages/lint` at `recordsOf`. Filed as a finding only, not claimed. #16910 is not addressed by this card.

## The declared contract

`collectFlowGraphs` (`packages/spec/src/automation/control-flow.zod.ts`) declares what it hands out:

```ts
function visit(
  nodes: readonly FlowNodeParsed[],
  edges: readonly FlowEdgeParsed[],
  ...
```

`FlowEdgeParsed` is a parsed edge record. The walk does not hold to it for `edges`.

## Measured — the node side is filtered, the edge side is forwarded

Around `:773`, the NODE side drops a member it cannot read (#16752):

```ts
const kept = nodes.filter((node) => isRegionDict(node));
graphs.push({ scope, path, nodes: kept.length === nodes.length ? nodes : kept, edges });
```

`edges` is pushed through untouched. And a nested region's edge list is admitted on `Array.isArray` alone, around `:786`:

```ts
Array.isArray(slot.raw.edges) ? (slot.raw.edges as FlowEdgeParsed[]) : [],
```

`Array.isArray` proves the LIST, never its MEMBERS. So a `body: { edges: [null, ...] }` — what a YAML `edges:` list item left empty deserialises to — becomes a `FlowGraph` whose `edges` array holds `null` while its declared element type says it cannot.

Reproduce, on `main`:

```ts
collectFlowGraphs({
  nodes: [
    { id: 'start', type: 'start', config: {} },
    { id: 'lp', type: 'loop', config: { collection: 'x', body: { nodes: [], edges: [null] } } },
  ],
  edges: [],
});
// the region graph's `edges` is [null] — declared FlowEdgeParsed[]
```

## Why this is not already closed by #16752

#16752 repaired this exact shape for `nodes`, at this exact producer, for this exact reason: a declared element type that lies is a contract the consumer cannot defend against, because no coercion at a call site can reach a list the producer reads out of a container's open `z.record` config. The repair was applied to one of the two lists the walk hands out. The edge side was not touched and still carries the producer's word about its members rather than a check.

## Reachability today — latent, not live

⛔ Do not read this as a crash report. #16910 re-pointed both `graph.edges` consumers in `packages/lint` (`lintFlowPatterns` and `validateStackExpressions`) at `recordsOf`, and the producer itself never dereferences an edge member — it only forwards them. So there is no reachable throw on the tree today, and the `packages/lint` family sweep is green in both directions at this addressing depth.

What is filed here is the contract lie, and the reason it matters is the one #15793 stated and #16752 acted on: a producer that hands out a member its declared type excludes puts every present and future consumer one unguarded dereference away from the crash, and the consumer coercion that currently saves us is belt, not braces. Remove either and the class re-opens — which is exactly the reading #16751's own note asks the reader not to collapse.

## Notes for whoever takes it

- The shape is settled by #16752's own repair one list over: filter the edge members the same way the node members are filtered, in the same walk, so `FlowGraph.edges` means what it says.
- ⚠️ Check what `analyzeRegion` (`:442`, `for (const e of edges)` reading `e.source` / `e.target` / `e.id`) does with a non-record member — it is a second consumer inside `packages/spec` itself, and it was not part of #16910's `packages/lint` surface.
- The pin belongs beside the existing ones: `packages/lint/src/non-record-object-entry.test.ts` already carries a `flows[].nodes[].config.body.edges` arm (added by #16910), so a producer-side repair is already observable from there; a `packages/spec`-side pin next to #16752's is the one still missing.
